items.title: Spearman's rank correlation goes from -1 to +1
items.claim: What does Spearman's rank correlation coefficient measure?

options.text: The strength and direction of monotonic association between ranked variables, between -1 (perfect negative) and +1 (perfect positive); 0 indicates no monotonic relationship
The mean of the two variables

items.reveal:
Spearman's ρ uses ranks rather than raw values, making it robust to outliers and non-linear monotonic relationships. Pearson's r requires a linear relationship and normally-distributed data.

Critical values must be checked against sample size: with n=10, ρ must exceed about 0.564 to be significant at p=0.05. With n=30, the threshold is about 0.306.

A strong correlation can be coincidental, confounded by a third variable, or reversed in direction (Simpson's paradox). 'Correlation does not imply causation' is a methodological starting point, not a slogan.
items.why: Statistical reasoning is part of geographical skills. Strong correlation is evidence, not proof — geographers must argue causation separately from association, ideally through mechanism.

items.title: A 4-figure grid reference is precise to 1 km; a 6-figure to 100 m
items.claim: What precision does each give on a UK Ordnance Survey map?

options.text: 4-figure references identify a 1 km × 1 km square; 6-figure references identify a 100 m × 100 m square. 8-figure references give 10 m precision
References are accurate to 1 metre regardless

items.reveal:
OS uses a National Grid: read eastings (left-right) first, then northings (bottom-up). 'Along the corridor, then up the stairs.'

Grid letters (SE, NY etc.) identify 100 km squares. A full reference combines letters with numerical eastings/northings — e.g. SE 5436 (4-figure within the SE square, locating a 1 km grid square; SE 543 367 for 6-figure 100 m precision).

The National Grid covers Great Britain only; Northern Ireland uses the Irish Grid. GPS coordinates (latitude/longitude or UTM) are international alternatives.
items.why: Map references are not arbitrary precision. Reporting weather or accident locations using inconsistent precision causes real navigation failures — including search-and-rescue.

items.title: The jet stream sits around 10 km above the surface

options.text: A surface wind near the equator
A narrow band of fast westerly winds (often 100-300 km/h) at around 9-12 km altitude (the tropopause), driven by temperature contrasts between polar and tropical air masses
An ocean current in the Pacific
A jet of supersonic air over deserts

items.reveal:
The polar jet (UK weather) and subtropical jet are the major Northern Hemisphere features. They meander in Rossby waves, and the shape of those waves controls where storm systems track.

Jet streams were discovered by Japanese balloon-bombing campaigns of WWII and by US bomber crews over the Pacific (1944) flying west into apparently impossible headwinds.

Arctic amplification (warming of the Arctic at roughly 4x the global rate) reduces the temperature contrast that drives the polar jet, possibly causing it to meander more — linked to more persistent weather extremes.
items.why: Surface weather has upper-atmosphere causes. Understanding why summer 2022 had heat domes or 2013-14 had stuck storm tracks requires looking at the jet.
